newsitem.title: USA: G7 to back trade gap curbs in Denver--U.S. Lipton.
newsitem.headline: G7 to back trade gap curbs in Denver--U.S. Lipton.

text.p: The Group of Seven is expected to back at this week's summit a broad commitment to promote sustainable economic growth and avoid excessive trade imbalances, a US Treasury official said on Tuesday.
Treasury Assistant Secretaty David Lipton told reporters that the commitment woud be a general statement, indicating that it would not single out any country, including Japan.
"We expect that you'll see an endorsement of a broad commitment among the G7 to pursue policies to promote sustainable growth and avoid excessive external imbalances," Lipton said.

President Clinton is expected to discuss the need for Japan to maintain strong domestic demand-led growth and avoid an unhealthy rise in its trade surplus when he meets his Japanese counterpart in Denver, Lipton said.
"This is a subject that will be discussed," he said.
Lipton touted America's economic success, calling economic conditions here the best in the industrial world.
By bringing down the budget deficit, the Clinton administration paved the way for lower U.S. interest rates and a strong dollar that have contributed to America's economic vigor, Lipton said.

"The steps that have been taken during the course of the Clinton administration to bring down the budget deficit have led to lower interest rates and a strong dollar and have all contributed to ... a strong economy," Lipton said.
"While economic performance in the United States has been strong," he added, "in many regions growth prospects are not so bright."
Lipton said he expects Europe's plans to forge a single currency to be discussed at the June 20-22 summit in Denver.
"The U.S. wants monetary union to proceed in a way that supports growth and stability in the region," he added.
The G7 summit will bring together the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin is also slated to attend all but one of the summit's meetings.
